hero.lead: {{app}} is the football app with purpose for every player, from grassroots to the professional game, and for the people who help them grow: coaches, analysts, clubs and federations. Sessions and a periodised week, matches, live analysis with the Njangi Index, video, and each player's journey, season after season.

train.title: Train
train.body: The method's 50 drills with their diagrams, sessions built in a few taps, the week from MD-4 to MD-1: fitted to the age group, the level and the fixture list, from U8 to the first team.

observe.title: Observe
observe.body: Tag the match from the touchline or on video, one tap per action. The Njangi Index tells you, from 0 to 100, whether the team kept the ball with purpose, and the report suggests next week's drills.

follow.title: Follow
follow.body: Each player's ten skills, matches, minutes and progress, season after season: the whole journey, from the first ball to the highest level.

njangi.title: Everyone pays in, the pot goes round, everyone benefits.
njangi.p1: In Cameroon, a njangi (also called a tontine) brings neighbours, colleagues and friends together. Each month, everyone puts their share into the same pot, and the whole pot goes to one member, in turn. Nobody keeps the money for themselves.
njangi.p2: On the pitch, the ball is the pot. The pass is the contribution. The goal is the pot paid out.
njangi.p3: But a pot that goes round without ever serving anything dies. So does possession without purpose. Keep the ball moving, yes, as long as it knows where it is going.

give.title: Everyone pays in
give.body: Every player shows for the ball, touches it, offers a solution.

circulate.title: The pot goes round
circulate.body: The ball goes through everyone and moves the opponent.

receive.title: Everyone benefits
receive.body: The circulation prepares something: a broken line, an entry, a goal.

njangi.figTitle: Six players pass the ball around a circle, each pass fills the pot, then the ball heads for goal.
njangi.figCaption: Six players, six touches: the pot fills up, then the ball heads for goal.

features.title: For all of football, from grassroots to the pros
features.lead: Pick your role: here is what {{app}} does for you.

lessons.title: Ball Lessons, for the youngest
lessons.body: For ages 8 to 12: 40 lessons from the {{series}} novel, each with its diagram, to understand the game by playing it.

challenges.title: Challenges and notebook
challenges.body: Challenges to do on your own, a notebook for what you learn, and a record of your progress between sessions.

skills.title: Your ten skills
skills.body: Scanning, first touch, passing with purpose, counter-pressing: where you stand, from 1 to 4, and what to work on now.

drills.title: Drills with diagrams
drills.body: Rondos, positional games, small and large-sided games, transitions, finishing. Filter by intention, age and day of the week.

builder.title: The session builder
builder.body: Put a session together in a few taps, or let {{app}} suggest one for the day and the age group.

week.title: The periodised week
week.body: From MD-4 to MD-1: tension, duration, speed, activation. The game model every day, the load at the right time.

match.title: Matches and lineups
match.body: Opponent, system, lineup on the pitch, a game plan for the four moments, call-ups by WhatsApp or SMS.

live.title: Live analysis
live.body: Tag the match from the touchline, one tap per action. The Njangi Index updates while you tag.

report.title: The match report
report.body: Score, Njangi Index and its five sub-indices, what worked, what to fix, and the drills for next week.

video.title: Video analysis
video.body: Load the video from your phone, mark the moments, draw on the frame to show little but show it right.

codes.title: The method's codes
codes.body: Progressive pass, line broken, box entry, regain within 5 seconds: the same codes as the book.

model.title: A shared game model
model.body: The same words and the same drills from U8 to the first team, even when the coach changes.

teams.title: All your teams
teams.body: One team per age group, from grassroots to the professional seniors, each with its sessions, matches and reports.

education.title: Coach education
education.body: {{methode}} as the basis for coaching courses: chapters, drill sheets, report templates.

plan2030.title: The 2030 plan
plan2030.body: Ten concrete measures for a federation, from the national model to child safeguarding.

journey.title: Your journey
journey.body: Every match, every minute, every assessment from your coach: your journey builds up season after season, from the U13s to the first team.

mola.title: Mola does the work. You stay in charge.
mola.p1: “Mola” means “mate” in Cameroonian camfranglais. It welcomes you by talking and fills in your profile as you chat. Then it acts in the app with the same tools you use.
mola.p2: Nothing goes out without your say-so: every message waits for your approval.

companions.title: Two books that go with the app
companions.lead: The Njangi Code gives coaches and analysts the method. Lionceaux tells it to children. Both are free to read online and to download as PDFs.

methode.label: The method book
methode.audience: For coaches and analysts, from grassroots to the professional game and national teams
methode.body: The African game model: the four moments, the five intentions of possession, the roles, the training week and periodisation, the Njangi Index and the match report, the 2030 plan for a federation. Its 50 drills and their diagrams are in the app.

series.label: The children's novel
series.meta: Novel, ages 8 to 12 · six books planned
series.body: Two Cameroonian brothers follow their parents from Douala to Maryland, then to France, Catalonia and London. In each country they learn one piece of football. Its 40 Ball Lessons are in the app's player space, for the youngest.

roadmap.title: 2030 or 2034: the countdown has started
roadmap.lead: Most of the players at those World Cups are between 14 and 26 today. They are already in our neighbourhoods, our academies and our diaspora.

a.title: Foundations
a.body: A written game model, books and an app to pass it on.

b.title: Alignment
b.body: Coaches trained in the same language, youth national teams aligned.

c.title: Competition
c.body: The World Cup in Morocco, Spain and Portugal, partly on African soil.

d.title: Summit
d.body: A star on the shirt. The dream come true.

series.meta: Novel, ages 8 to 12 · six books planned
series.shelfLead: Six books that follow the two brothers from the neighbourhood pitch to the World Cup. Book 1 is out, the next ones are being written.

tome1.body: Kaydoudou, 11, the number 8 who sees everything. BriBri, 10, the winger with odd socks. The two brothers leave the red earth of Bonamoussadi to follow their parents to the United States, France, Spain and England. In each country they learn one piece of football, and the old ball stitched back together by their grandmother Mami Nyanga travels with them.
tome1.partsTitle: Five countries, five pieces of the Njangi

1.idea: We play together, everyone pays in.

3.idea: See before you receive, win it back fast.

4.idea: Be in the right place, build triangles.

5.idea: Keep the ball even when it burns.
